description: The declared surface of the third artifact of TALOS_INSIMUL_BRIDGE.md §7.5 — which TBP verbs this bridge answers from the knowledge base, which node groups carry the answers, and the why-not token every other verb is refused with. DATA, because §7.5's whole point is that the bridge wraps Insimul's API and neither project depends on the other: nothing here names a Talos symbol, and nothing in addons/insimul/ reads this file.

carrier.finding: hello_response.schema.json declares `capabilities` with additionalProperties:false and rejects unknown keys BY DESIGN, so the payload this bridge assembles has nowhere to travel on the wire until Talos registers the namespaced block in an additive minor (BRIDGE §7.9 ask 2, REFUSE_AT_HELLO.md 'The carrier does not exist yet').
carrier.carried_meanwhile_as: the `insimul.capabilities` watch key of talos.game.yaml — the one channel tbp/1.x already has for a game-declared value.

checkpoint.note: Tier 1, never tier 2. A KB snapshot restores the SIMULATION and not the SCENE — transform, animation, agent path and physics are host-side by the same decision that makes core portable — so `checkpoint_fidelity: kb_authoritative` is declared beside the tier and a tier-2 claim is not made.

markers.maps: a KB query for generated places, whose entity ids are stable across regenerations from one seed (BRIDGE §3.5)
markers.note: Talos's instrumentation contract item 6 is runtime marker registration for procgen. Here the marker set is a byproduct of generation, so announcing is a query rather than an authoring task. Navmesh validation stays host-side.

readiness.maps: KB liveness plus the refuse-at-hello decision (BRIDGE §7.5, §7.7)
readiness.note: The §7.5 rule lives here: the adapter never reads the KB at construction, so this answers false until a world is live and every state verb before that is refused as insimul_kb_uninitialized rather than answered with an empty success.

rng.maps: the world seed — generation is measured deterministic end to end from it (BRIDGE §3.7)
rng.note: Seeding is a world-generation input, so a reseed after a world is open is recorded and reported rather than silently applied to a world that was not built from it.

contexts.maps: the host's game-state PHASE — never Insimul's @world(W) context (BRIDGE §3.8)
contexts.note: The name collision §3.8 defuses: Talos's context is a phase enum that gates detectors; Insimul's context is the KINP world layer truth is true IN. This bridge says `phase` for the first and `@world` for the second, and never the bare word for either.

events.maps: KB deltas — quest state, death, and schema-invalid facts (BRIDGE §3.8)
events.note: The events Talos names are already state transitions in an Insimul game, so the stream is a KB delta feed rather than new instrumentation. assert_failed is the gift: a schema-invalid fact reaching the KB is a game bug no ordinary target can even see.

inject_input.mapping: the three-level consumption echo is the engine's; Insimul can add a fourth level below it
inject_input.trap: Injecting at Insimul's action layer bypasses the engine's input pipeline entirely, which is the one thing inject_input exists to test (BRIDGE §3.3). This bridge refuses rather than manufacturing the false green.

probe_injection_paths.mapping: input paths are host concerns by construction

execute_skill.mapping: the predicate half of hold_until_predicate is a Prolog goal; the controllers are not Insimul's

query_state.mapping: a Prolog query over the live KB, canonically sorted before the digest cap (BRIDGE §3.4)

query_objects.mapping: the scene walk is host work; Insimul supplies the stable entity id that resolves into the KB

save_checkpoint.mapping: insimul_kb_snapshot, stamped with the four axes (BRIDGE §3.5, §7.7)

restore_checkpoint.mapping: insimul_kb_restore, refused when the archive stamp does not match the published matrix

teleport.mapping: generated markers with stable entity ids; navmesh validation stays host-side

set_progress_var.mapping: insimul_assert against a schema-validated predicate, routed through the promotion path (BRIDGE §3.6)

play_input_trace.mapping: the portable input-trace artifact (tasklist 180) is the better oracle; TBP refuses a foreign-session trace_ref by design (RISK-60)

step_frames.mapping: nothing on a per-frame path crosses the C ABI, so core has no clock to step

load_level.mapping: playthrough load plus an entry marker

screenshot.mapping: nothing in Insimul touches pixels — core's tsconfig omits the dom lib on purpose

mark_event.mapping: a KB delta on the events channel (BRIDGE §3.8)

run_native_test.mapping: this repo's in-engine gates are conformance harnesses rather than gdUnit4/GUT suites, so they need the sibling run_conformance convention of BRIDGE §3.10

declare_context.mapping: the host PHASE, published on the contexts channel — never Insimul's @world (BRIDGE §3.8)

insimul_verb_host_owned.means: the verb is the engine host's job and the knowledge base has no reading for it. Not a gap in the install — a gap in what a KB is
insimul_verb_host_owned.unblock: let the Talos Bridge answer this verb; the Insimul profile should not plan it against the KB

insimul_verb_unmapped.means: the verb is within Insimul's reach and this artifact does not map it yet. Named apart from host_owned because the two have different fixes: one is a design boundary, the other is work
insimul_verb_unmapped.unblock: map the verb in addons/insimul_talos/bridge-contract.json and implement its hook

insimul_verb_unknown.means: a verb this contract does not declare at all. Under absent-means-absent semantics a typo is indistinguishable from a decision, so an undeclared verb is refused rather than guessed at
insimul_verb_unknown.unblock: check the verb against TBP v1's inventory (talos:docs/03-engine-bridge.md §2.3)

insimul_kb_uninitialized.means: a state verb arrived before a world was loaded. BRIDGE §7.5: the adapter never reads the KB at construction, and an empty solution set read as 'no facts' is the silent degradation this rule exists to eliminate
insimul_kb_uninitialized.unblock: wait for talos_ready_state() to report ready, then retry — this is a warm-up, not a refusal to serve

insimul_world_template_write_refused.means: a set_progress_var targeting a world TEMPLATE. Asserted runtime facts belong in save.currentState.prologFacts via the promotion pipeline; a write to a template would corrupt every future playthrough of that world, invisibly (BRIDGE §3.6)
insimul_world_template_write_refused.unblock: target the playthrough's own state, not the world template

insimul_module_inactive.means: the verb is about a module this world's genre bundle never activated. capabilities.insimul.active_modules is what makes this 'not applicable' rather than 'unresponsive' (BRIDGE §3.1, §7.8)
insimul_module_inactive.unblock: plan against a world whose genre activates the module, or drop the objective

insimul_bridge_not_configured.means: the bridge was asked to decide before it was handed its contract and its matrix. A half-present install answers nothing rather than degrading to a default (BRIDGE §7.8)
insimul_bridge_not_configured.unblock: install addons/insimul_talos in full — bridge-contract.json and supported-versions.json ship with the addon

hello_tokens.note: The 42-token hello/restore vocabulary is the workspace's, not this artifact's. tools/verify-talos-bridge/check-bridge.mjs fails when this bridge can emit a hello-stage token the published matrix does not carry — the same rule the reference implementation's selftest applies (docs/REFUSE_AT_HELLO.md).
